title: Part B of the R6B results connection: a results panel on the website behind its own off-by-default website switch that POSTs to the already-accepted route /api/v1/properties/{bbl}/results for one lot, shows each result settled / conditional / withheld (a withheld value shows its reason and never a number, an older value or a substitute), offers the design choices as visible editable starting values and the special-density statement as a statement the user may make (never pre-filled, never a fact), and handles switch-off / loading / each typed server answer / network failure / a document that fails the website's own check; it changes NO server file, turns NO production switch on, and adds NO report page, PDF, estimator or option comparison (serves D-090-R228/R229/R240/R255/R256/R258/R267-R269/R292/R548/R556/R569/R570/R582/R584/R588 and ADR-007; acts on DB-180, DB-196(c), DB-199(e), DB-202(f); stands on M5-T139 for the entered height; leaves DB-199(d), DB-203 and DB-204(b)(c) to server tasks)
objective:
Build the results panel on the website. It is the first screen that shows the results. It changes NO server file and turns NO production switch on.

READINGS (a drafting helper read the code at head d1b488cb; the orchestrator checked them at the claim base; each is a reading: verify it in the source before relying on it). Reading: the three server pieces are merged - the results document in its three-way form (packages/contracts/schemas/v1/results.schema.json, contract 1.3.0), the lot's five conditions come from evidence (M5-T137), and the route POST /api/v1/properties/{bbl}/results behind INTERNAL_RESULTS_ENABLED, off by default (services/api/app/api/v1/results_read.py:264). Reading: the display layer already exists and already renders settled / conditional / withheld - the reader apps/web/src/lib/architect/three-answers.ts (answerView at :232 shows a conditional value's 'If ...' line via conditionLine at :225, and a withheld value as its reason via WithheldValueView at :183, NEVER falling back to another value - the headline-withheld branch at :276) and the cards apps/web/src/components/architect/answers/AnswerCard.tsx (WithheldLine at :116 prints 'Not known - <reason>' and no number; ConditionNote at :133), ThreeAnswersPanel.tsx (:39), ScopeSummary.tsx, ResultsStatusStrip.tsx. Reading: a dashboard tool is added as a member of DASHBOARD_TOOLS with a TOOL_LABELS and TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS entry (apps/web/src/components/architect/workspace/types.ts:3-36), a case in DashboardTools.tsx (:68) that returns the real panel when its boolean prop is set else <PlannedView/>, the boolean threaded through LoadedDashboard and DashboardEntry (apps/web/src/components/architect/workspace/DashboardEntry.tsx:34,115) and read on the server page apps/web/src/app/property/workspace/page.tsx:25 (NOT src/app/property/page.tsx - that is the ArchitectEntry surface; this is a reading to confirm). Reading: an opener button is offered in DashboardPanels.tsx gated by the same boolean (pattern of proposalEditorEnabled at :201). Reading: a website switch is a server-read, default-off flag reader like apps/web/src/lib/architect/proposal-editor-flag.ts (TRUE_TOKENS, never NEXT_PUBLIC_, read once on the server page and passed down as a plain boolean); the name is INTERNAL_RESULTS_UI_ENABLED (ruling R1), DISTINCT from the server's INTERNAL_RESULTS_ENABLED; the existing readers of the same kind are apps/web/src/lib/architect/parity-panel-ui-flag.ts and hidden-issue-flags-ui-flag.ts. Reading: a typed client copies apps/web/src/lib/study/study-setup-api.ts (fetchStudySetup returns a discriminated union of outcomes; fetchImpl injection; a timeout; 404->not_available, 422->validation_error, 503->inputs_unavailable, 500->internal_*, network/timeout/abort/unexpected); the results route adds ONE more 503 state, lot_conditions_unconfirmed (results_read.py:123 RESULTS_READ_STATUS_STATE_MATRIX). Reading: the browser harness apps/web/e2e/harness/fixture_api.py mounts the REAL route offline by injecting its provider (get_results_study_inputs_provider) and setting INTERNAL_RESULTS_ENABLED + LANE_A_ENABLED for the harness process only (the study-read pattern at fixture_api.py:515); no response byte is hand-written. Reading: the flag-on journey runs against the :3001 server in apps/web/playwright.config.ts (chromium-flag-on project); the website switch env is set there. Reading: component tests load the committed document through apps/web/src/test-support/results-fixtures.ts (loadResultsFixture). Reading: the committed journey document is packages/contracts/fixtures/valid/results/recorded_215_16_northern_journey.json.

STEP 1 - the client and the switch. Write apps/web/src/lib/results-api.ts: a typed POST client fetchResults(bbl, body, {fetchImpl, timeoutMs}) returning a discriminated union of outcomes, one per row of the server matrix - success(document) for 200, not_available for 404, validation_error (carry code + field) for 422 validation_error, rate_limited for 429, inputs_unavailable for 503 inputs_unavailable, lot_conditions_unconfirmed for 503 lot_conditions_unconfirmed, internal_error / internal_contract_error for the two 500 states, plus network_error, client_timeout, aborted, unexpected_response, and validation_failure when the 200 body fails the website's own check (a handwritten check in its own module, apps/web/src/lib/results-contract-checks.ts, by the pattern of apps/web/src/lib/hidden-issue-flags-contract-checks.ts and of validateStudySetupDocument in apps/web/src/lib/study/study-setup-api.ts; ruling R9; no new package). The body carries only {housing_program, floor_to_floor_ft?, special_density_statement?} (results_request.py:47-55). Write apps/web/src/lib/architect/results-ui-flag.ts: the default-off website switch reader (proposal-editor-flag.ts shape; ruling R1).

STEP 2 - the panel and the wiring. Write apps/web/src/components/architect/ResultsPanel.tsx: it offers the design choices and the statement (the form is its own file, apps/web/src/components/architect/ResultsForm.tsx), asks the server ONLY when the user presses the button (ruling R2), shows the state, then renders the existing ThreeAnswersPanel over the returned document (showDraftValues on - this is a lane-flag surface). The form: (i) housing program - the three the server accepts (standard_residence | qualifying_affordable_housing | qualifying_senior_housing), shown as the user's choice of option; (ii) floor-to-floor height - an editable field that is empty at the start (ruling R3); (iii) the special-density statement - an optional statement the user may make, NEVER pre-filled and NEVER shown as a fact, with text that it is the user's statement. A request made without an entered height and without the statement carries housing_program only: floor_to_floor_ft and special_density_statement are OMITTED (the server then uses its starting height and the returned document's line shows it and calls it the default). Thread the website switch: add 'results' to types.ts (DASHBOARD_TOOLS + a TOOL_LABELS 'Results' + a TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS line), add a case 'results' in DashboardTools.tsx (props.resultsUiEnabled ? <ResultsPanel bbl={bbl}/> : <PlannedView label={TOOL_LABELS.results}/>), thread resultsUiEnabled through DashboardEntry.tsx and DashboardPanels.tsx (add a 'Results' opener button gated by the flag), and read the flag on apps/web/src/app/property/workspace/page.tsx. The new prop is OPTIONAL wherever it is added and is false when absent (as parityUiEnabled is in DashboardPanels.tsx), so no existing caller and no existing test changes; the pages apps/web/src/app/property/page.tsx, compare/page.tsx and confirm/page.tsx, ArchitectEntry.tsx and ArchitectShell.tsx are NOT touched. Update the one tool-set test apps/web/src/components/architect/workspace/__tests__/floating-workspace-window.test.tsx. Add the browser harness wiring to apps/web/e2e/harness/fixture_api.py and the :3001 env to apps/web/playwright.config.ts.

EVERY TOP-LEVEL BLOCK OF THE RESULTS DOCUMENT AND WHAT THE PANEL SHOWS (schema required[]+generated type; confirmed field-by-field). The panel's reader consumes exactly the Pick in three-answers.ts:35 (out_of_date, out_of_date_reason, lot_selection_statement, with_approvals_label, answers, remaining_floor_area, shortfall, completeness_line, status_strip, notices_count, draft, street_width_case, scope); it renders no other block. Table (block | shown):
contract_version | not shown; the client requires 1.3.0 for the three-way layer (internal).
results_id / study_id / option_id / revision / computed_at / depends_on_fact_ids | not shown (internal ids/time).
out_of_date + out_of_date_reason | shown in the status-strip details ('Out of date - <reason>') when true; fixture false -> nothing.
lot_selection_statement | shown in the status-strip details (the 'Based on the lots you selected ...' line).
with_approvals_label | shown in the strip details when non-null; fixture null -> nothing.
answers.floor_area_allowance | the Floor-area allowance card: headline + rows with each conditional 'If ...' line; the three legal_unit_limit_* shown as withheld reasons (no number).
answers.permitted_envelope | the Permitted envelope card: six heights conditional; max_lot_coverage, rear_yard, setback_above_base shown as withheld reasons.
answers.building_option | 'Not available - <reason>' (whole not_available answer; reason only, no number).
remaining_floor_area | supplement row under the allowance card: 'Remaining development capacity: Not confirmed' + reason (fixture not_available).
shortfall | block under the building-option card: 'Not available - <reason>' (fixture not_available).
addon_gains | NOT shown (carries engine internal words 'task A-12','this slice'; DB-199(e)); the completeness_line already names the uncovered add-ons in plain words.
best_combination | NOT shown.
completeness_line | shown: completeness_line.text as the completeness paragraph.
status_strip | shown as the document has it, unchanged: up to three items + overflow in details; its first item reads 'Zoning maximum' (the server's words; ruling R5).
notices_count | shown: 'Notes (N)' in the strip details when > 0.
floor_by_floor | NOT shown (empty in fixture; a later-milestone table).
floor_stack | NOT shown.
existing_building | NOT shown (carries internal 'task M2-08').
unit_estimate | NOT shown (the realistic apartment estimate is a later milestone; R569 - the legal limit is shown separately as a withheld/conditional value under the allowance).
geometry | NOT shown by this numbers panel (drawings are a later milestone).
rule_versions | NOT shown as a list (DB-202(f): it still names the coverage rule while coverage is withheld, so it must not be shown as 'the rules behind the shown results'); per-value zr_sections still show under 'Rule sections'.
draft | consumed, not displayed: draft true + showDraftValues controls whether numbers show (lane-flag surface shows them under the 'internal preview, rules not reviewed' tag).
street_width_case | shown in the strip details as plain lines when present; fixture null -> nothing.
scope | shown via ScopeSummary: label, lot display, 12 assumption rows (key/value/basis/statement), whole-site statement, remaining-capacity label + reason.
No block is left out.

THE STATES AND WHAT THE USER SEES (one test each). switch off (website flag off): no call is made, the tool shows the plain 'not available' view. switch on, before the user asks: the form and its button; no result; no call. loading (after the button): a working/busy state. a result shown and an input changed since: the line of ruling R3. success (200): the panel renders. 404: 'not available' / not connected (route switched off on the server). 422 validation_error: 'the request could not be understood' and, for a form-field code, the field's message (codes: invalid_body, field_not_accepted, housing_program_required/invalid, floor_to_floor_ft_invalid, special_density_statement_invalid, body_too_large, invalid_json; plus a malformed BBL). 429 rate_limited: 'too many requests - try again shortly' + retry. 503 inputs_unavailable: 'the results could not be loaded right now; safe to retry' + retry. 503 lot_conditions_unconfirmed: the server's plain reason, NOT labelled safe to retry. 500 internal_error / internal_contract_error: a plain 'something went wrong' (no stack, no path). network failure: 'could not reach the server' + retry. a document that fails the website's own check: a 'could not be loaded' state; no partial or garbled document is rendered.

THE RULES THE DISPLAY MUST KEEP (each with a test). A withheld value shows its reason and never a number, an older value or a substitute (R556, R570; red/green on the reader's headline-withheld branch). A withheld value says whether it is missing information or work still owed (R258 - gap_kind in plain words; the reader must carry gap_kind into the withheld view and the card must print it; ruling R6). A legal limit and an estimated apartment count never share a label (R569 - the legal limit shows under 'Legal dwelling-unit limit'; the unit_estimate block is not shown). A conditional result shows its conditions (R268). Nothing is called the maximum for the property and no height is settled while the K20 conditions are not checked (R269, R267). No option is presented as feasible and a line reads 'parking, loading and bicycle requirements: not yet checked for this option' (R548; DB-180). The standing not-reviewed label is on the screen exactly once (ADR-007; the dashboard already renders StandingReviewLabel once - the panel must NOT add a second copy).

THE INPUTS. housing program: the three above; a visible choice (the user's option). floor-to-floor height: an editable field, empty at the start, with its helper line (feet; a positive finite number; rulings R3 and R4). special-density statement: an optional statement (true = 'the lot is NOT in a special density area'); never pre-filled; shown with text that it is the user's statement, not a fact; sent only when made.

BACKLOG ROWS. ACT ON: DB-180 (add the parking/loading/bicycle 'not yet checked' line - a display line; capturing the provisions is owed research, not this task). DB-196(c) (blocks worked out from conditional results must be labelled conditional or not shown - this task does NOT show addon_gains / best_combination / floor_stack / geometry / unit_estimate, so none appears without its conditions; a test asserts they are absent). DB-199(d) ('Zoning maximum' on the strip - ruling R5; keep the document's text verbatim, add a test that NO value label or headline reads 'maximum for this property'). DB-199(e) (engine internal-word texts must not reach the screen - this task does not render the blocks that carry them; add a text-guard test that none of 'this slice','Lane A','task A-12','not encoded','not_available','rule_not' appears in the rendered panel). DB-202(f) (do not present rule_versions as 'the rules behind the shown results' - not shown). DONE ON THE SERVER BEFORE THIS TASK: DB-204(a) (task M5-T139: through the route an entered height's line says 'A 14-foot floor-to-floor height was entered for this run.', a selected program's line says '... was selected for this run as the housing program.', and the starting height is still called the default). NEEDS A SERVER CHANGE, NOT IN THIS TASK: DB-199(d) (the wording of the status strip's first item), DB-203 (a lot with no geometry gets a 503 - fine for the benchmark lot which has geometry, but real lots need the server fix), DB-204(b) (no sign-in protection; the switch stays off until sign-in exists - blocker B-001), DB-204(c) (no upper limit on the height - a product decision not made; the website invents none: ruling R4).

THE BROWSER AND COMPONENT TESTS. W-1 (results-api.test.ts, WIRING): each server answer maps to its outcome (success, not_available, validation_error+code, rate_limited, inputs_unavailable, lot_conditions_unconfirmed, internal_error, internal_contract_error, network_error, client_timeout, aborted, unexpected_response, validation_failure) via an injected fetchImpl. W-2 (results-panel.test.tsx, WIRING): load the committed journey document through loadResultsFixture; walk EVERY settled value, EVERY conditional 'If ...' line and EVERY 'not known' on the cards and assert each equals the document; nothing retyped. W-3 (results-panel.test.tsx, WIRING): the states above - loading; switch off (no call); a fact not given (its results withheld, the rest shown, no fact pre-filled); before the user asks (the form, no call); the housing program visible with its starting choice and editable; the height field empty at the start with its helper line, and editable; the special-density statement empty by default; a result shown and an input changed since (ruling R3); each server error. W-4 (results-panel.test.tsx, WIRING): the standing label appears once on the surface. W-5 (results.flag-on.spec.ts, LAW): the flag-on browser journey - open the lot (BBL 4073340070), open the Results tool, press the button, observe the REAL POST to :8000 returning 200; the height's line calls the starting height the default; entering 14 and pressing again returns the line that says a 14-foot height was entered, and the housing-program line names the program the form shows, in the form's own words (ruling R3); the heights appear as the district's limits with the values of reference-case Table A (base 30/45, building 55; qualifying 65), conditional, naming the unchecked conditions, and NOWHERE called the maximum for the property; the floor-area figures (20,150 / 24,180 sq ft) appear conditional naming the recorded-area condition; coverage, rear yard and building option read 'not known'; making the density statement makes the standard legal unit limit (reference-case L6: 29) appear as a conditional result naming that statement, never settled. EXPECTED VALUES COME FROM docs/reference-cases/R6B/cases/ (step R0), not from the recorded answer. results.spec.ts: the flag-off default - no opener, no call, the plain 'not available' view. W-6 (results-panel.test.tsx / the flag-on spec, WIRING): keyboard + screen-reader checks as the existing tool suite does (Escape closes the window and returns focus to the opener; the panel has an accessible name). Every test is marked [LAW] or [WIRING]; a withheld result has a test it reads 'not known'; a conditional result has a test it is labelled and names its assumption; one red/green proof on the withheld-no-fallback guard; one mutation proof per pinned branch (e.g. flip the density statement and prove ONLY the unit limit's way changes - R292).

FILES OUTSIDE apps/web: none. The e2e harness (apps/web/e2e/harness/fixture_api.py) and the Playwright config (apps/web/playwright.config.ts) are both under apps/web. The harness imports from services/api and reads the committed fixture under packages/ READ-ONLY; it edits neither. If the orchestrator finds the website switch needs a server file, a schema, a packages/ fixture, a dependency file, tools/, .github/, .claude/ or render.yaml, that is a QUESTION and must not go in the paths; a new package is out of the question.

NOT IN THIS TASK: no server file change (no route, no engine, no contract, no schema, no fixture under packages/); no production switch turned on (the website switch and INTERNAL_RESULTS_ENABLED stay off by default); no report page; no PDF; no realistic apartment-count estimator; no option comparison; no drawing or 3D; no change to the rule tables, render.yaml, CI config or dependency files. The DB-203 lot-without-geometry fix, sign-in (DB-204(b)), a height upper limit (DB-204(c)) and the rewording of the status strip's first item on the server (DB-199(d)) are separate tasks.

RULINGS OF THE ORCHESTRATOR. They settle the draft's open questions. None is the builder's to change; a ruling that cannot be built as written is a STOP and a report, not a different choice.

R1 THE WEBSITE SWITCH. Name: INTERNAL_RESULTS_UI_ENABLED. Reader: resultsUiEnabled() in apps/web/src/lib/architect/results-ui-flag.ts, the shape of proposal-editor-flag.ts: only an explicit true token turns it on; absent, empty or unknown is off; never prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_; read once on the server page apps/web/src/app/property/workspace/page.tsx and passed down as a plain boolean. In apps/web/playwright.config.ts it is set ONLY on the :3001 server. The harness sets the SERVER's switches for its own process only, as it does for the study read.

R2 NO REQUEST BEFORE THE USER ASKS. With the switch on and the tool open the panel shows the form and ONE button, 'Show results'. It makes no call on mount, on open or when an input changes. It calls when the user presses the button: one request, built from the form as it stands. Reason: the returned document says the housing program 'was selected for this run'; that is true only of a run the user asked for. A newer request aborts an older one still in flight; an older answer is never shown after a newer one (one test).

R3 THE TWO DESIGN CHOICES AND WHAT THE SCREEN SAYS OF THEM. Housing program: the three the server accepts, in the words the server's own line uses ('Standard residence', and the two others as the returned line prints them: read them from the server's transform, services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/three_way_document.py, and prove in the flag-on journey that the form's label of the chosen program is the name in the returned line); standard residence is the visible starting choice. Floor-to-floor height: the field is EMPTY at the start, with the helper line 'Leave empty to use the program's starting height. The height used is shown with the results.' The website holds NO copy of the server's starting height: no constant, no placeholder number. An entered height is sent, in feet. After a result is shown, the document's own two lines (the scope summary) say which program and which height were used and on what basis; the form must never contradict them. So: when any input differs from the inputs the shown result was asked with, a plain line stands above the result: 'You changed an input. These results are for the earlier inputs. Press Show results to update.' (one test: change an input after a result; the line appears; the shown numbers do not change until the button is pressed).

R4 THE HEIGHT'S CHECK MIRRORS THE SERVER: a positive, finite number. The website invents NO upper limit (backlog row DB-204 c). A value the form refuses is not sent; its message: 'Enter a height in feet greater than zero.' A value the server refuses shows the server's own field message.

R5 THE STATUS STRIP IS SHOWN AS THE DOCUMENT HAS IT. The website does not hide, reorder, replace or restyle an item of it; its first item reads 'Zoning maximum'. Those are the server's words (services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/explanations.py, build_status_strip) and the product plan's label for this kind of answer; whether they stay beside conditional values is a server question on record (backlog row DB-199 d), owed before the website switch is turned on anywhere, and NOT this task's. This task's share of rows R267 and R269: every conditional value shows its 'If ...' line; no value label, headline or line the WEBSITE writes calls a value the maximum for the property, a confirmed maximum, or feasible (one test over the whole rendered panel; the settled words 'Remaining development capacity: Not confirmed' are the document's and stay as they are).

R6 THE KIND OF GAP (row R258). A withheld value, and a whole answer that is not available and carries a gap_kind, say which of the two kinds they are, after the reason, in these words: missing_information -> 'Missing information about this property.'; work_owed -> 'Not built yet: this part of the program is still owed.' The words live in ONE place (apps/web/src/lib/architect/three-answers.ts), keyed by the document's gap_kind. A gap_kind that is absent, null or unknown to the website shows NO kind line and never a machine word. The withheld view (WithheldValueView) carries the kind; apps/web/src/components/architect/answers/AnswerCard.tsx prints it. The reader's own test apps/web/src/lib/architect/__tests__/three-answers.test.ts compares the withheld view by exact equality (its line 180) and is among the allowed paths for that reason. The blocks that use the shared not-available shape without a gap_kind (remaining_floor_area, shortfall) show none (backlog row DB-196).

R7 THE PARKING LINE (row R548, backlog row DB-180), exact words: 'Parking, loading and bicycle requirements are not yet checked for this option. It is not shown as feasible.' It is shown whenever a result is shown.

R8 THE STANDING LABEL: the dashboard renders it once; the panel adds none (one test counts it on the surface with the tool open).

R9 WHERE THE CODE GOES. apps/web/src/lib/results-api.ts (the typed client; the pattern of apps/web/src/lib/study/study-setup-api.ts). apps/web/src/lib/results-contract-checks.ts (the website's own check of a returned document, handwritten, no new package): at least contract_version 1.3.0; every field the reader consumes present and of its kind; every value_states entry one of the three ways with its required fields; and it REFUSES a document in which a key is withheld in value_states and also present among the answer's values (so a number can never be shown for a withheld result even if a server erred; one test). apps/web/src/lib/architect/results-ui-flag.ts. apps/web/src/components/architect/ResultsPanel.tsx (asks, states, result) and ResultsForm.tsx (the three inputs and the button). apps/web/src/components/architect/results-panel.css (layout of the form and the states only; use the existing global classes first: card, section-note, primary-button, secondary-button, architect-eyebrow). The threading test: apps/web/src/components/architect/workspace/__tests__/dashboard-results-flag.test.tsx (switch off or absent: no opener, the tool shows the plain not-available view, no call is made; switch on: the opener is there and the tool shows the form), by the pattern of dashboard-proposal-flag.test.tsx.

R10 THE REPORT LISTS EVERY TEXT THE WEBSITE WRITES for this panel, each with the state that shows it. Each is plain and true: no internal name, no machine word, no pull-request or task number, nothing about which law text is captured or built, never 'professional review', never 'unsupported'.

COULD TWO THINGS ON THIS SCREEN DISAGREE? The builder answers this in the report for: the form against the shown result (R3); the form's program label against the returned line (R3); a withheld value against any number elsewhere on the panel (R9's refusal; the reader's guard); the kind-of-gap words against the reason beside them (R6); the status strip against the conditional values (R5: stated, not solved here).
business_reason: The owner's goal is the full feasibility report with reliable numbers (R588). Step 4 of the owner's sequence is to connect one option to the screen and prove that a changed input changes every result that depends on it (R292), after the pieces that emit the results document are merged (R582). This task is that first screen: it shows the results the server already works out, each as settled, conditional or withheld, behind a website switch that is off by default; it turns no production switch on (R584).

Any schema or fixture under packages/contracts (read-only).
render.yaml, .github/, .claude/, tools/, and any dependency file (package.json, package-lock.json).
Any production environment or switch default (INTERNAL_RESULTS_ENABLED and the new website switch stay off by default).
